Missing data: bounded FIML

Source: vignettes/articles/model-fiml.qmd

Models › Clusters and latent variables › Missing data: bounded FIML

Keep partly observed rows instead of deleting them. Part of the Models collection.

Status: these models are numerically verified against lavaan, not statistically admitted: no interval coverage is established, and every source_fit interval route is refused (medfit_error_fiml_inference_unavailable).

Structure X to M to Y, two parallel mediators, or two serial mediators (the saturated graph or the pure chain), each with no, one or two covariates
Class returned FIMLMediationData (simple), FIMLParallelMediationData (parallel) and FIMLSerialMediationData (serial)
Route fit_sem(model, data, missing = "fiml", fixed_x = FALSE) then extract_mediation(), or fit_mediation(engine = "sem", engine_args = list(missing = "fiml", ...))
Standard errors observed information, model-based; delta-method effect intervals
Availability simple model from 0.16.0; covariates, parallel and serial forms from 0.17.0

What it is, and what it assumes

Ordinary fits delete every row with a missing value on a model variable. Full-information maximum likelihood (FIML) keeps a row that has at least one observed model variable and uses what it has. It assumes the variables are jointly normal and that the missingness is ignorable under that model (missing at random). It does not impute values, and a fixed pattern of missing values in a real study is not evidence that missingness is ignorable.

The opt-in is deliberately narrow and explicit. It requires continuous X, M and Y, independent Gaussian disturbances, free intercepts, fixed_x = FALSE, meanstructure = TRUE, observed information and model-based standard errors. A failed FIML fit never falls back to listwise deletion or to another engine.

A simple example 

d <- withr::with_seed(271L, {
  n <- 400L
  x <- .8 + stats::rnorm(n, sd = 1.1)
  m <- -.4 + .5 * x + stats::rnorm(n, sd = .8)
  y <- .7 + .6 * m + .25 * x + stats::rnorm(n, sd = .9)
  data.frame(treatment = x, mediator1 = m, outcome = y)
})
d$mediator1[seq(1, nrow(d), by = 7)] <- NA_real_
syntax <- "mediator1 ~ a*treatment
outcome ~ b*mediator1 + cp*treatment"
fit <- fit_sem(syntax, d, missing = "fiml", fixed_x = FALSE,
               meanstructure = TRUE, information = "observed", se_type = "model")
nobs(fit)   # every row with an observed model variable is kept
[1] 400
z <- extract_mediation(fit, treatment = "treatment", mediator = "mediator1")
tidy(z, type = "effects")
# A tibble: 3 × 3
  term  estimate std_error
  <chr>    <dbl>     <dbl>
1 nie      0.279    0.0365
2 nde      0.247    0.0508
3 te       0.527    0.0457

Which models are covered

Model Covariates Notes
X, M, Y 0, 1 or 2 direct path free or fixed at exactly zero
Two parallel mediators 0, 1 or 2 the mediator disturbances independent (M1 ~~ 0*M2) or free
Two serial mediators, saturated 0, 1 or 2 both shortcut paths X -> M2 and M1 -> Y written and free
Two serial mediators, pure chain 0, 1 or 2 both shortcut paths absent; a restriction the data can reject

In the serial forms all three disturbance covariances (M1 ~~ 0*M2, M1 ~~ 0*Y, M2 ~~ 0*Y) must be written. With covariates, every covariate predicts every equation and the exogenous covariances are all written or none. The syntax rules, parameter counts and the extraction details are in the sem engine guide.

In a serial fit, extract_mediation() names both mediators in the fitted order. In the pure chain the treatment is the variable with no path to the second mediator, so a covariate cannot be named as the treatment there. In the saturated graph any exogenous variable may be the treatment when no direct path is fixed, and a direct path fixed at zero marks the treatment. print() and summary() of a serial FIML object name the variant and the covariates.

What is not available

  • Case weights, fit tests (anova()), profiles and MBCO.
  • Source-fit bootstrap intervals: bootstrap_mediation(source_fit = ...) is implemented but withheld until statistical admission, and raises medfit_error_fiml_inference_unavailable. Delta-method (normal) intervals from tidy() and confint() are available.
  • quick(), pm() and glance() on an extracted FIML object.
  • Three or more covariates, three or more mediators, constraints, ties, bounds, latent variables, factors and products.

Evidence

The fits are compared with lavaan raw-data FIML (and OpenMx on one cell per form) on complete, missing-completely-at-random, missing-at-random and sparse patterns, with an independent likelihood check and planted-defect tests (the fiml and fiml-ext simulation gates). Nothing here is a coverage claim for intervals under missing data.
